statement.en: This level is set at Peggy's Cove, on the Atlantic coast of Nova Scotia. Discover Canada says the Bay of Fundy has the world's highest tides. It says the province's identity is tied to shipbuilding, fisheries and shipping.
statement.fr: Ce niveau se déroule à Peggy's Cove, sur la côte atlantique de la Nouvelle-Écosse. Discover Canada dit que la baie de Fundy a les plus hautes marées du monde. Le guide dit aussi que l'identité de la province tient à la construction navale, à la pêche et au transport maritime.

source.quote: Known for the world’s highest tides in the Bay of Fundy, the province’s identity is linked to shipbuilding, fisheries and shipping.

verification.evidence: Known for the world’s highest tides in the Bay of Fundy, the province’s identity is linked to shipbuilding, fisheries and shipping. … Picture: (Right) Peggy’s Cove harbour, Nova Scotia

blurb.en: Three oceans touch Canada: the Pacific in the west, the Atlantic in the east, and the Arctic in the north. This bare rock is the Atlantic edge.
blurb.fr: Trois océans bordent le Canada : le Pacifique à l'ouest, l'Atlantique à l'est et l'Arctique au nord. Cette roche nue, c'est la bordure de l'Atlantique.

source.quote: Three oceans line Canada's frontiers: the Pacific Ocean in the west, the Atlantic Ocean in the east, and the Arctic Ocean to the north.

verification.evidence: Three oceans line Canada’s frontiers: the Pacific Ocean in the west, the Atlantic Ocean in the east, and the Arctic Ocean to the north.

blurb.en: This is Peggy's Point Lighthouse. Nova Scotia's identity is linked to building ships, to fishing and to shipping.
blurb.fr: Voici le phare de Peggy's Point. L'identité de la Nouvelle-Écosse est liée à la construction navale, à la pêche et au transport maritime.

source.quote: Nova Scotia is the most populous Atlantic Province, with a rich history as the gateway to Canada. Known for the world’s highest tides in the Bay of Fundy, the province’s identity is linked to shipbuilding, fisheries and shipping.

verification.evidence: Nova Scotia is the most populous Atlantic Province, with a rich history as the gateway to Canada. Known for the world’s highest tides in the Bay of Fundy, the province’s identity is linked to shipbuilding, fisheries and shipping.

blurb.en: Much of Atlantic Canada's history comes from its coastline and its natural resources. Fishing, farming, forestry and mining built these provinces and gave them a big place in the country's story.
blurb.fr: Une grande partie de l'histoire du Canada atlantique vient de son littoral et de ses ressources naturelles. La pêche, l'agriculture, la foresterie et l'exploitation minière ont bâti ces provinces et leur ont donné une grande place dans l'histoire du pays.

source.quote: Atlantic Canada's coasts and natural resources, including fishing, farming, forestry and mining, have made these provinces an important part of Canada's history and development.

verification.evidence: Atlantic Canada’s coasts and natural resources, including fishing, farming, forestry and mining, have made these provinces an important part of Canada’s history and development. … the province has long been known for its fisheries, coastal fishing villages and distinct culture. … Nova Scotia has a long history of coal mining, forestry and agriculture. … Forestry, agriculture, fisheries, mining, food processing and tourism are the principal industries.

blurb.en: Most Canadians live in cities. Canadians also live in small towns, in the countryside, and everywhere in between.
blurb.fr: La plupart des Canadiens vivent dans des villes. Des Canadiens vivent aussi dans de petites localités, à la campagne, et partout entre les deux.

source.quote: While the majority live in cities, Canadians also live in small towns, rural areas and everywhere in between.

verification.evidence: Population Canada has a population of about 34 million people. While the majority live in cities, Canadians also live in small towns, rural areas and everywhere in between.
